title: "Healthcare Access"
subtitle: "Family doctors, unmet needs, and emergency department utilisation"
---

```{python}
#| echo: false
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "docs/assets")
from portal_helpers import load, fig_defaults, kpi_row, data_note, COLORS
import plotly.graph_objects as go
import pandas as pd

data = load("healthcare_access")
```

Access to primary care is a fundamental determinant of health system performance.
This section examines provincial variation in family physician access, unmet care needs,
and emergency room utilisation.

---

::: {.section-header}
## Provincial comparison
*Family doctor coverage and unmet care needs by province*
:::

```{python}

prov_df = pd.DataFrame(data["by_province"]).sort_values("pct_family_doctor", ascending=True)

fig = go.Figure()
fig.add_trace(go.Bar(
    name="Has Family Doctor",
    x=prov_df["pct_family_doctor"],
    y=prov_df["province"],
    orientation="h",
    marker_color=COLORS["primary"],
    opacity=0.85,  # <-- Added here
    hovertemplate="%{y}: %{x:.1f}%<extra>Family Doctor</extra>",
))
fig.add_trace(go.Bar(
    name="Unmet Care Need",
    x=prov_df["pct_unmet_need"],
    y=prov_df["province"],
    orientation="h",
    marker_color=COLORS["danger"],
    opacity=0.85,  # <-- Added here
    hovertemplate="%{y}: %{x:.1f}%<extra>Unmet Need</extra>",
))
fig.update_layout(
    barmode="overlay",
    xaxis_title="% of respondents",
    yaxis=dict(tickfont=dict(size=12)),
    # opacity removed from here
)
fig_defaults(fig, "Family Doctor Access & Unmet Need by Province", height=480).show()
```

---

::: {.section-header}
## Emergency room visits — distribution
*Visits in the past 12 months*
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
er_df = pd.DataFrame(data["er_distribution"])

fig = go.Figure(go.Bar(
    x=[f"{v} visit{'s' if v != 1 else ''}" for v in er_df["visits"]],
    y=er_df["pct"],
    marker_color=[
        COLORS["success"] if v == 0 else
        COLORS["warning"] if v <= 2 else
        COLORS["danger"]
        for v in er_df["visits"]
    ],
    text=[f"{p}%" for p in er_df["pct"]],
    textposition="outside",
    hovertemplate="%{x}: %{y:.1f}%<extra></extra>",
))
fig.update_layout(yaxis_title="% of respondents", xaxis_title="ER visits (past 12 months)")
fig_defaults(fig, "Emergency Room Visit Distribution", height=380).show()
```

---

::: {.section-header}
## Unmet care need by income
*Lower-income respondents disproportionately report unmet needs*
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
unmet_df = pd.DataFrame(data["unmet_by_income"])
income_order = ["Under $30K", "$30K–$59K", "$60K–$99K", "$100K–$149K", "$150K+"]
unmet_df["income_bracket"] = pd.Categorical(
    unmet_df["income_bracket"], categories=income_order, ordered=True
)
unmet_df = unmet_df.sort_values("income_bracket")

fig = go.Figure(go.Scatter(
    x=unmet_df["income_bracket"],
    y=unmet_df["pct_unmet_need"],
    mode="lines+markers",
    line=dict(color=COLORS["danger"], width=3),
    marker=dict(size=10, color=COLORS["danger"]),
    fill="tozeroy",
    fillcolor="rgba(192,57,43,0.1)",
    hovertemplate="%{x}: %{y:.1f}% unmet need<extra></extra>",
))
fig.update_layout(
    yaxis_title="% with unmet care need",
    xaxis_title="Household income",
)
fig_defaults(fig, "Unmet Care Need by Income Bracket", height=360).show()
```

::: {.stat-callout}
The income gradient in unmet care is stark: respondents earning **under $30K** are
roughly **3–4× more likely** to report an unmet healthcare need than those earning **$150K+**.
:::
